records.name_en: Sensirion SHT85 Temperature and Humidity Sensor
records.description_en: A digital sensor for measuring temperature and relative humidity in laboratory environments, with dew point estimation based on the measured values. It supports multiple repeatability modes, periodic asynchronous acquisition, ART for faster humidity response, and an internal heater for debugging, typically integrated through an I2C interface.
A single channel of the Vescent Photonics Slice-DHV piezo driver, used in experiments for independent control of a piezo actuator to support precision positioning or tuning applications.
A short-wave infrared imaging camera used to acquire sample images in the SWIR range, commonly used for material identification, sorting, agricultural inspection, and research imaging experiments.

A multi-channel excitation light source system for microscopy and fluorescence experiments. It connects over a serial port and manages multiple color channels. Individual channels may correspond to LEDs, luminescent light pipes, or lasers to provide illumination at different wavelengths.

records.name_en: Sunbrick Multi-Channel Tunable Spectrum LED Light Module
records.description_en: The Sunbrick is a multi-channel, networkable LED light module that allows per-channel output control, overall intensity adjustment, preset spectrum loading, and node temperature monitoring. It is used in laboratories to provide programmable and repeatable illumination for optical testing, material characterization, and other experiments requiring tunable spectral lighting.

The Sutter Lambda 10-3 is a high-performance multi-filter wheel controller for microscopy and optical imaging workflows. It supports synchronized control of up to three filter wheels and shutters for rapid filter switching and excitation/emission path management.

A Sutter motion device used for microstep-resolution linear positioning of samples, probes, or optical components in laboratory experiments. It supports initialization and shutdown, command/reply communication, position readback, absolute/relative moves, and homing.

A temperature controller for the HCP TC038D oven. It communicates via Modbus raw bytes to read registers, write parameters, set the temperature setpoint, and monitor the current temperature for laboratory heating and temperature regulation.

Temperature control and status interface for the HCP TC038 laboratory oven. It can read the current temperature, set the temperature setpoint, configure monitored registers, and query device information for oven heating control and monitoring.

The Thorlabs TC200 is a laboratory temperature controller that drives a heating element, reads temperature from a thermistor, and uses PID regulation to hold the temperature at a setpoint. It is used for sample heating, thermal stabilization, and temperature management in optical or electromechanical experiments.

A USB-connected temperature sensing device used in laboratory setups to measure ambient temperature or temperature near a sample. Depending on the model, it may support 1 to 2 sensor channels, and some variants can also report humidity and apply calibration scale and offset.

The TOPTICA iBeam is a compact smart diode laser source with serial control for laser on/off operation, output power setting, and status readback. It is commonly used for microscope excitation, optical experiments, and other laboratory applications requiring stable continuous laser output.

A controllable laser light source for laboratory optical experiments, supporting laser emission on/off control and output power set/readback. It is suitable for applications such as microscopy and excitation illumination.
A device entry for TI DLP digital micromirror devices (DMDs), typically paired with DLPC controllers.
TI DLPC900 is a programmable controller for DMDs such as DLP6500, supporting high-speed pattern control for advanced light control.

A single-channel control interface for Thorlabs APT piezo device controllers, used to operate piezo stages or piezo inertia actuator channels, including enable control, drive and jog parameter configuration, position readback, absolute moves, jog motion, and homing for laboratory positioning tasks.

records.name_en: Thorlabs APT Piezo Inertia Actuator Controller
records.description_en: A multi-channel controller for Thorlabs piezo inertia actuators, typically including devices such as the KIM101. It enables single- or multi-axis actuators, supports step motion, absolute positioning, and drive parameter configuration, and is commonly used for fine positioning and alignment of optics, mirror mounts, and precision translation mechanisms in laboratory setups.

A controller for Thorlabs APT-compatible motorized stages, rotation stages, and other precision motion mechanisms. It supports homing, absolute/relative moves, jog motion, and position/status readback, and is commonly used for precise positioning, alignment, and scanning in optical experiments.

A non-physical software component for communicating with Thorlabs APT motion-stage controllers. It sends and receives protocol messages over a serial-style port, runs the message-processing loop, exposes the file descriptor, and retrieves controller serial number, channel count, and connected stage information for automation workflows involving single-controller or card-slot controllers.

A laboratory multi-channel LED illumination controller used to manage LED light sources. It supports connecting to the device, switching individual channels on or off, setting and reading brightness, and querying serial number, firmware, and manufacturer information. It is suitable for microscopy and other experimental illumination applications.
A motorized filter wheel for microscope and other optical beam paths, used to switch between multiple filter positions to select the desired optical filter and query the current wheel position.

A motorized filter wheel for controlling Thorlabs FW102C and related models, used in microscopy and optical experiments to switch between filter positions. It enables rapid selection of filters in the optical path for fluorescence imaging and general optical measurements.

A high-level control interface for a Timepix/Medipix pixel detector. It supports configuring pixel thresholds, masks, test pulses, and multiple DAC bias parameters, as well as device setup, acquisition start/stop, data recording, and Ethernet communication settings for radiation detection, particle imaging, and time-related measurements.

An acquisition system for connecting to SPIDR and initializing and controlling one or more Timepix pixel detectors. It supports bias voltage control, starting and stopping acquisition, receiving data by polling or callback, and recording acquired data to files.

Controls a Timepix4 pixel detector for laboratory data acquisition, including loading configuration, setting pixel threshold/mask/test parameters, managing Ethernet data filtering, and starting, stopping, and recording detector data.

A laboratory light source controlled over USB-TMC communication, supporting on/off control, intensity setting, runtime setting, status queries, temperature readout, and preset recipe activation for lab illumination, excitation, or timed exposure tasks.

This is a non-physical software helper component that reads Hamilton VENUS laboratory automation resource files, such as deck layouts, liquid class databases, and submethod libraries, and converts them into Python classes for reuse in automation scripts and workflow definitions.

A non-physical software component for Raman experiment demonstration. It parses command-line arguments, connects to a laser driver board and an IDS camera, and coordinates spectrum or image acquisition in a run loop, optionally firing the laser and saving data files and PNG outputs.
A camera/acquisition interface driver component for the X-Spectrum LAMBDA 750K detector imaging chain, used for laboratory image acquisition and data readout.

records.name_en: XCalibur Syringe Pump with Distribution Valve
records.description_en: An XCalibur syringe pump for laboratory fluid routing and precise aspiration/dispensing. It controls absolute/relative plunger motion, valve port switching, motion speeds, microstepping, and command sequences, and supports waste dispensing, line priming, and initialization for automated sample transfer, priming, and fluid handling.

The Newport XPS is a laboratory motion controller used to operate motorized stages, positioning platforms, and other precision motion hardware. It is commonly used in optical experiments, automated measurements, and precision positioning systems, and supports network-based control as well as reading and writing configuration or script files stored on the controller.

This is a multi-channel LED light controller used to drive and control LED illumination channels in microscopy and optical experiments. It serves as an illumination control unit for independently managed LEDs, suitable for fluorescence excitation, transmitted/reflected illumination, and multi-wavelength optical setups.

A single motion axis of a Zaber ASCII-controlled motorized stage or linear actuator, used in laboratories for precise positioning of samples, optical components, or probes, including homing, relative/absolute moves, and velocity control.

This is a precision motorized positioning device controlled over a serial ASCII protocol, typically with one or more motion axes for homing, absolute moves, relative moves, and continuous motion. It is commonly used in laboratories for precise positioning and automated scanning of samples, optical components, probes, or fixtures.

This is a motorized positioning device, typically a single-axis or multi-axis stage, controlled over a serial ASCII protocol. It supports homing, absolute moves, relative moves, constant-velocity motion, and stopping, and is used in laboratories for precise positioning, scanning, and alignment of optics, samples, or probes.

This is a motorized precision positioning stage or single-axis motion platform used for accurate linear positioning and automated motion control. It is commonly used in laboratories to position optical components, samples, or probes, including homing, point-to-point moves, and automated scanning.

An integrated multi-laser light source that combines multiple laser channels in one unit with centralized output control. It is commonly used for microscopy, fluorescence excitation, and other experiments requiring multi-wavelength laser illumination.

This is a digital motion controller for closed-loop control of DC and brushless motors, with communication over CANopen, USB, or RS232. It supports position, velocity, and current control and is commonly used for precision positioning and actuator control in laboratory and automation systems.

A non-physical desktop GUI software component for UV-Vis spectral acquisition and display in laboratory experiments. It can connect to UC480 cameras or Ocean Optics spectral input devices, perform real-time readout, wavelength-axis handling, exposure and gain adjustment, dark subtraction, averaging/recording, curve plotting, and data save/load operations.

Controls an rLINE electronic pipette for aspiration, dispensing, blowout, tip ejection, homing, and reset, while reading position and level feedback for automated laboratory liquid-handling workflows.

A programmable collaborative robot arm that can be controlled through block-based programs or Python scripts for motion sequences, joint movements, and experimental operations. It is commonly used for teaching, laboratory automation, sample handling, and robot workflow development.

The xArm collaborative robotic arm is a multi-joint robot used in laboratory automation for sample transfer, positioning, gripping, and repetitive handling tasks. The device can report Cartesian position, joint status, operating mode, alarms, temperature, and motor-related states, making it suitable for automated operations and process monitoring.

A collaborative robot for laboratory automation that supports joint and Cartesian motion, trajectory recording and playback, and control of grippers, tool/controller I/O, Modbus peripherals, and force-torque sensing and force-control functions.

A programmable multi-axis robotic arm that can execute motion tasks from G-code or predefined paths. In laboratories, it is commonly used for automated pick-and-place, sample transfer, positioning, and repeatable motion workflows.

This is an example PLC-controlled 3-axis motion stage with simulated X, Y, and Z motion and several discrete state positions. It is mainly used in laboratory or beamline control environments to demonstrate and test motion control, limit behavior, state changes, and integration with higher-level control systems.

A general-purpose laboratory I/O controller that communicates over a serial port and provides channel-based digital output, analog output, analog readback, and temperature readout. It is commonly used in microscopes and other experimental setups for peripheral coordination, sensor acquisition, and simple actuator control.

This is a general-purpose laboratory I/O controller that communicates over a serial port. It provides digital outputs, analog outputs, flash/pulse-style control, servo control, and analog and temperature readback. It is commonly used for peripheral coordination and automation in microscopes and other lab setups, such as driving shutters, laser-related components, shaking mechanisms, or reading sensor signals.

A laboratory automation robotic arm and gripper system for Cartesian linear motion, motion completion waiting, and gripper open/close control, suitable for sample pick-and-place, transfer, and handling tasks.

A beam diagnostics profile intensity monitor. It inserts or retracts a YAG target or diode into the beam path via a Y-axis mechanism, and uses zoom optics with an area detector to observe beam profile and intensity distribution; some variants also include focus control or LED illumination.

A fiber shaker is a laboratory device that mechanically vibrates an optical fiber. It is commonly used in laser illumination paths to reduce speckle and improve illumination uniformity, especially in microscopy and other optical experiments.

A handheld game controller used as a human input device for robot teleoperation in the lab. Joysticks, triggers, bumpers, and buttons are mapped to 6-degree-of-freedom motion increments and gripper control, making it suitable for manual teaching and real-time control of a robot arm or end effector.

This is a software data storage component for microscopy acquisition workflows. It stores multidimensional images and their metadata in RAM and indexes them by coordinates such as channel, z, time, position, row, and column for fast checking, retrieval of image data, and retrieval of metadata during experiments.

records.name_en: Variable-Temperature Experiment Control Backend and GUI Component
records.description_en: A non-physical software component that coordinates connection, configuration, temperature ramp control, measurement acquisition, and GUI state management for a Keithley 2400, Keithley 2182, and Lakeshore 350 in variable-temperature electrical measurement workflows.

A precision syringe pump for liquid delivery, controllable over a serial connection with pump addressing on a daisy chain. It supports setting syringe diameter, flow rate, and target volume, and performing infusion, withdrawal, and stop operations for microfluidics, metered dispensing, and flow experiments.

A graphic annotation and region-of-interest (ROI) object used in scientific imaging software. It can represent overlays such as rectangles, ellipses, lines, points, rings, and wedges, and is typically used on microscopy images or spectra for region selection, measurement, mask generation, interactive editing, and annotation.

A non-physical software component that simulates a two-support/two-jack vertical mirror for experiment control. It converts between raw actuator values and derived mirror parameters, and allows the mirror state to be set using derived targets, making it useful for testing control logic and coordinate transforms.

A motor-driven multi-axis precision translation device that supports absolute/relative motion, homing, defining a home position, and unit selection. It is commonly used for precise positioning, scanning, and alignment of microscope objectives or samples.

The BX2A is an Olympus microscope body/stand that serves as the main platform for the optical, illumination, and motion components of a microscope. In laboratory use it supports core observation and imaging tasks. Based on the exposed controls, the body supports lamp status management, Z-axis positioning, motion-state reporting, and soft-limit and origin settings for routine microscopy workflows.

A research-grade Olympus IX/BX microscope body that manages illumination status and controls objective/focus Z-axis motion and limits for laboratory sample observation, focusing, and microscopy imaging.

A halogen illumination source for the Olympus IX81 inverted microscope, providing visible-light illumination for sample observation and commonly used for routine microscopy and focusing in brightfield or transmitted-light imaging.

An Andor scientific camera is a high-sensitivity laboratory detector, typically with thermoelectric cooling, used for low-light detection and spectral acquisition. Based on the available evidence, it supports integration time, shutter, fan, high-gain mode, vertical binning, and detector temperature control, and is commonly used as the detector in research spectroscopy systems.

This is not a physical lab instrument but a software rule object for microscopy data processing. It monitors incoming frames and event data, prepares result files and metadata, and triggers or advances localization analysis once data acquisition is complete, typically in microscope image localization or cluster-based analysis workflows.

A laboratory imaging camera system used for image acquisition in lab setups. It can discover and connect cameras, perform single or multi-frame capture, provide image buffers and device metadata, and support field-of-view, focal length, calibration, and low-level register/memory access. This device class may include visible-light cameras as well as thermal or hyperspectral cameras.
